message.content: {"drafts":[{"title":"Choosing Between API and Local LLMs for Generating Game Character Content in an iOS App","body":"An iOS developer is exploring adding a feature to generate game character details like backstory and stats using LLMs, not conversational AI. They are weighing whether to use API-based services like OpenAI, Claude, or Gemini, or run a local LLM on the device. The trade-offs include avoiding user friction from login and API management versus the potential increase in app size and performance hits from local models. There's also uncertainty about whether fine-tuning is necessary and how to prepare a model for deployment. Additionally, they want to limit the model's output to exclude sexual or controversial content. Given these considerations, what practical advice or examples exist for selecting and preparing LLMs for this kind of mobile content generation? Are there known approaches to efficiently restrict model outputs in this context?","fact_refs":["F1","F2","F3","F4","F5","F6"]},{"title":"Integrating LLMs for Game Character Content in Mobile Apps: General Discussion","body":"A developer is interested in adding LLM-generated content features to a mobile app, focusing on game character information like backstory and stats. They are considering both API-based and local LLM options and are concerned about user experience factors such as setup complexity, app size, and performance. Questions include whether fine-tuning is required and how to limit the model's functionality to avoid inappropriate content.
